Write a bash script that renders a config template.

Starting files:
--- /home/eval/app/app.conf.tmpl ---
# generated for ${APP_ENV}
[db]
host = ${DB_HOST}
port = ${DB_PORT}
url = postgres://${DB_USER}@${DB_HOST}:${DB_PORT}/app
[runtime]
home = ${RUNTIME_HOME}
greeting = Hello, ${USER_NAME}!
price = $5 per unit
--- end ---
--- /home/eval/app/prod.env ---
# production settings
APP_ENV=prod/eu
DB_HOST=db.internal
DB_PORT=5432

DB_USER=app_rw
UNUSED_KEY=x
--- end ---

Render /home/eval/app/app.conf.tmpl into /home/eval/app/app.conf:
- `prod.env` holds `KEY=VALUE` lines; blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored. Values are taken literally (they may contain `/`).
- Every `${NAME}` placeholder whose NAME is defined in prod.env is replaced by its value.
- Placeholders whose NAME is not defined in prod.env stay exactly as written, even if a variable of that name exists in the shell environment.
- Everything else (including `$5`) is copied unchanged.

Then print one line to stdout: `unresolved: ` followed by the names of the placeholders left unresolved, sorted, unique, space-separated (here: `unresolved: RUNTIME_HOME USER_NAME`). Exit 0.

transcript.final_response:
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

TMPL=/home/eval/app/app.conf.tmpl
ENVFILE=/home/eval/app/prod.env
OUT=/home/eval/app/app.conf

# Parse KEY=VALUE lines, skipping blanks and comments.
declare -A env=()
while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n $line ]]; do
    [[ -z $line ]] && continue
    [[ $line == '#'* ]] && continue
    [[ $line == *=* ]] || continue
    key=${line%%=*}
    val=${line#*=}
    env[$key]=$val
done < "$ENVFILE"

# Read the template, preserving any trailing newline.
content=$(cat "$TMPL"; printf x)
content=${content%x}

# Replace ${NAME} only when NAME is defined in prod.env.
declare -A unres=()
re='\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}'
out=
rest=$content
while [[ $rest =~ $re ]]; do
    m=${BASH_REMATCH[0]}
    name=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
    out+=${rest%%"$m"*}
    if [[ ${env[$name]+set} ]]; then
        out+=${env[$name]}
    else
        out+=$m
        unres[$name]=1
    fi
    rest=${rest#*"$m"}
done
out+=$rest

printf '%s' "$out" > "$OUT"

# Report unresolved placeholder names, sorted and unique.
printf 'unresolved:'
if ((${#unres[@]})); then
    mapfile -t sorted < <(printf '%s\n' "${!unres[@]}" | LC_ALL=C sort)
    for n in "${sorted[@]}"; do
        printf ' %s' "$n"
    done
fi
printf '\n'

exit 0
```
